verdict.rationale: AWS's Bedrock AgentCore is explicitly positioned as a platform for deploying and running AI agents in production that call tools/APIs autonomously, with built-in auth handling and step-by-step observability, and it supports major agent frameworks (LangChain, OpenAI Agents SDK, etc.). Combined with general automation infrastructure (CLI scripting, CloudFormation/CDK for provisioning), this supports building autonomous background automations, but the evidence lacks concrete scheduling/triggering mechanisms (e.g., EventBridge cron, Lambda triggers) or a hands-on example of an agent actually running unattended in the background over time. Missing for 10: evidence of scheduling/trigger primitives for autonomous runs, and independent/hands-on confirmation that AgentCore-deployed agents run reliably unattended.
